findings.contract: Safe SSL context replacement retains message observer and must not abort
findings.cause: SSL copies the callback pointer from original context at construction; set_SSL_CTX changes current context without changing callback pointer. Trampoline looks up original F in current context and expects it.
findings.reproduction: Create cert-bearing context B without observer, create SSL from A with message observer, switch to B before or during valid SNI handshake, then complete real peer handshake. First callback lookup in B panics in extern C and aborts.
findings.remedy: Resolve message F through existing owned original context retained in SESSION_CTX_INDEX, preserving current-context SslRef inspection; no silent skip.
findings.controls: Observe actual valid handshake messages before/after context switch; retain ordinary observer/keyupdate control and verify original context remains live after caller drops it.
findings.status: source-supported, sent to integration owner; no runtime execution
findings.regression: Real safe server-name callback switches from context A with observer to keyed B without observer during a TLS 1.3 handshake; independent atomic records messages after successful switch, and client/server exchange full request/response application bytes. Isolated baseline process abort is pending integration-owner execution.
